description: §18.5 block-arm value lowering when the block's TAIL EXPRESSION is an identifier merely PREFIXED by a statement keyword (`formatted` starts with `for`, `doc` with `do`, `letter` with `let`, `constant` with `const`, `online` with `on`). The statement-head classifier that decides whether a block's last segment is the arm's result carried its word boundary INSIDE the keyword alternation, so it fenced only `on` and every other keyword matched as a bare prefix. Such a tail was misclassified as a statement, was never lifted to the enclosing result var, and the arm silently produced `null`. Both consumers of the classifier are pinned here: the structured/variant-arm path and the raw/literal-arm path.
rationale: §18.5: "A block arm is `{ statement* expression? }`. The block's result is its **last expression**." and "A block arm body's result type SHALL be the type of its last expression." An identifier that merely begins with the letters of a keyword is an EXPRESSION, not a statement, so it is the block's result. `tintVariant(.Low)` -> "amber" (tail `formatted + "ber"`), `tintVariant(.High)` -> "indigo" (tail `doc + "digo"`), `tintLiteral(1)` -> "violet" (tail `letter + "olet"`), `tintLiteral(2)` -> "teal" (tail `constant + "al"`), `tintLiteral(9)` -> "gray" (bare non-block arm, unaffected). `tintOnPrefixed(1)` -> "scarlet" pins the ONE keyword that already carried a boundary as UNCHANGED. `statementTail(1)` -> "" pins the other direction of §18.5: a block whose last segment is an assignment STATEMENT has no trailing expression, so the arm produces void and the interpolation renders empty. Pre-fix the four keyword-prefixed anchors all rendered empty (silent-wrong, no diagnostic); `base`/`b`-named tails passed, which is why the defect shipped. `tintDollar(1)` -> "magenta" and `tintDollar(2)` -> "cyan" pin the `$` CONTINUATION: scrml identifiers admit `$` (`isIdentPart = /[A-Za-z0-9_$]/`) but JS `\b` is defined against `\w` = [A-Za-z0-9_], which excludes `$` — so a `\b`-based fence still reads `do$thing` and `on$c` as keyword-then-boundary and reproduces the defect, including for `on`. The fence is therefore matched to the language's own identifier charset, not to `\w`. Measured at authoring time: zero corpus identifiers of the form <keyword>$..., though `$`-bearing identifiers (`item$`, `acc_$`, `_$1`) are in live corpus use — so this pins a reachable class with no current instance, closed at the root rather than at twelve positions.
